transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I just don’t feel any interest in the community projects and hobbies that used to mean everything to me. I used to be so active with my walking tours, the community garden, and church, but now I just can't find the heart to do any of it. It all just feels completely blank to me now.

Have you had other periods in your life, lasting at least two weeks, when you felt this same loss of interest or depression before this current episode? Or did this begin only after a specific stressful life event or major change?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life; I used to be so active and social, and I absolutely loved my community projects. This complete loss of interest and heavy sadness started right after that horrible accident at the crosswalk two years ago, and it hasn't let up since.

Since the crosswalk accident, do upsetting memories or nightmares about it keep coming back, or do you avoid reminders of what happened? Have you also felt constantly on edge or easily startled since then?

Yes, I'm constantly plagued by vivid memories of that day—especially when I hear screeching tires—so I take the long way around town just to avoid that intersection. I also feel incredibly on edge, watching cars like a hawk before I step off any curb and always needing to face the door in cafes so I can see everything around me.

Since the accident, have there been times when you felt detached from yourself or like the world around you wasn’t real? Do you also have any gaps in your memory for important parts of what happened during or right after the accident?

No, I don't have any gaps in my memory; in fact, I remember every single detail of that day all too well. I also haven't felt like I was detached from my own body or that the world around me wasn't real.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a clear traumatic event (crosswalk accident) followed by persistent re-experiencing, avoidance, and hyperarousal symptoms lasting for two years, with associated loss of interest in previously valued activities. There is no evidence of dissociative symptoms or amnesia, and the symptom pattern is most consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder.
